paragraphs: Nayoti. In Shabbat 121b he killed a snake on Shabbat. Rashi explains that he was Jewish and was called after his place.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The supplied heading ניותי is provisionally transliterated Nayoti; earlier machine גיותי has gimel. Both source כשבת spellings are read contextually as בשבת, in Shabbat for the citation and on Shabbat for the act. The Hebrew is unchanged; older machine בשבת/בשבה remains historical evidence.

קכא: gives Shabbat 121b under the colon convention, without independent named-edition verification. The Jewish status and place-derived designation are Hyman’s attribution to Rashi, not a fresh identification. No personal title is added.
